symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of vertices in the fixed experimental network.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: A generic label, with \(a=1\) denoting the focal exposure and \(a=0\) denoting the comparison exposure.

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: The fixed adjacency matrix on the \(n\) experimental units.

symbols.name: \nu
symbols.def: The randomization distribution chosen before outcomes are observed.

symbols.name: f_i
symbols.def: The exposure mapping induced by \(G\) for unit \(i\).

symbols.name: Y_i(w)
symbols.def: The potential outcome of unit \(i\) under assignment \(w\).

symbols.name: \Pi
symbols.def: The diagonal matrix whose diagonal is \((\pi_{1,1},\ldots,\pi_{n,1},\pi_{1,0},\ldots,\pi_{n,0})\).

symbols.name: Y_i(a)
symbols.def: The potential outcome of unit \(i\) under exposure label \(a\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: The superpopulation law of the pair \((Y_i(1),Y_i(0))\) used only for ex ante basis choice.

symbols.name: F_a^{-1}
symbols.def: The generalized inverse of the marginal distribution function.

symbols.name: b_1
symbols.def: The coefficients multiplying the focal-exposure indicators.

symbols.name: b_0
symbols.def: The coefficients multiplying the comparison-exposure indicators.

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: A fixed lower bound on the normalized smallest eigenvalue of \(S_B\).

symbols.name: \mathcal B_Z
symbols.def: The scale-quotiented block-separable bases for which \(S_B\) is positive definite.

symbols.name: g_B(c)
symbols.def: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), the Zhao gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right]\).

symbols.name: \ell_B(c)
symbols.def: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), the residual \(\ell_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]-g_B(c)\).

symbols.name: m_a
symbols.def: The number of independent unpaired pilot outcomes observed under exposure label \(a\).

symbols.name: Y^{P}_{j,a}
symbols.def: The \(j\)-th independent pilot draw from \(F_a\), with no cross-arm pairing.

symbols.name: \widehat r(B)
symbols.def: The diagnostic obtained by substituting empirical marginal moments and endpoints into \(r(B)\).

symbols.name: \widehat v
symbols.def: The diagnostic value \(\widehat v=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\).

symbols.name: \widehat{\mathcal A}_R
symbols.def: The diagnostic set \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}
symbols.def: An exact rational or real-algebraic encoding, or certified inclusion-oracle encoding with effective refinement moduli and exact feasibility decisions, of the known design matrices, both endpoint moment matrices, endpoint covariances, regularity threshold, and tolerance.

symbols.name: h_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: The maximum projective-chart diameter of a box retained at tolerance \(\varepsilon\).

symbols.name: \xi
symbols.def: The instance \(\xi=(\nu,F_1,F_0)\) with \(G\) and the exposure maps held fixed.

symbols.name: \mathfrak X_\kappa
symbols.def: The relatively topologized class of instances satisfying the named predicates ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility.

symbols.name: B_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: An exactly feasible basis used to certify an upper bound on \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\).

symbols.name: L_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: A rational lower bound on \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) obtained from outward-rounded lower bounds over all retained feasible boxes.

symbols.name: U_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: A rational upper bound on \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) certified by an exactly feasible incumbent and outward rounding.

symbols.name: \mathcal C_\varepsilon
symbols.def: The union of unpruned quotient-chart boxes, required to contain \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\).

symbols.name: \mathscr K_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: A checkable record of the chart cover, feasible incumbent, minimization bounds, retained outer boxes, exact infeasibility or lower-bound pruning records, and mesh.

symbols.name: \delta
symbols.def: A positive certified lower bound on \(\Delta(\xi)\).

symbols.name: \eta
symbols.def: A uniform positive lower bound on normalized nondegeneracy above \(\kappa\) over \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\cup\mathcal A_0\).

symbols.name: \widehat w(B)
symbols.def: The endpoint residual criterion obtained by substituting the empirical marginal moments and Frechet covariance endpoints into \(w(B)\).

assumptions.condition: For every unit \(i\) and assignments \(w,w'\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(f_i(w)=f_i(w')\) implies \(Y_i(w)=Y_i(w')\).
For every unit \(i\) and label \(a\in\mathbb A\), \(\pi_{i,a}>0\).
The \(n\) pairs \((Y_i(1),Y_i(0))\) have joint law \(H^{\otimes n}\).

standard.name: Independent and identically distributed potential-outcome pairs, Zhao Assumption 3\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 22

assumptions.condition: The law \(H\) assigns probability one to \([0,1]^2\).
The ordered pair of marginals of \(H\) equals \((F_1,F_0)\).
The feasible covariance image satisfies \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\).

standard.name: Sharp Fréchet covariance range, Aronow--Green--Lee Lemma 1

assumptions.condition: The pair \(\left(F_1\otimes F_0,\operatorname{Cov}_{F_1\otimes F_0}\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}\right)\) belongs to \(\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\times\{0\}\).

standard.name: Independent product coupling with zero covariance
Supplied-basis control-variate nondegeneracy, Zhao Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 21

assumptions.condition: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).

novel.justification: Independent rescaling of either basis column leaves Zhao's control-variate span and gain unchanged, so this condition selects compact representatives without restricting implementable estimators.

standard.name: Supplied-basis nondegeneracy, fixed-threshold variant of Zhao Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 21

assumptions.condition: There exist vectors \(b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n\) and \(\lambda_{\min}\{n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B\}\ge\kappa\) for \(B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix}\).

novel.justification: This is a verifiable design-side condition: for a fixed network, exposure maps, and known randomization, the matrix \(\Omega\) is known before outcomes are observed, so nonemptiness of the normalized \(\kappa\)-regular projective class can be certified as part of design preparation. Zhao's Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) regulates a supplied basis and does not assert existence of such a normalized feasible basis.

assumptions.condition: The two arm-specific pilot samples are mutually unpaired i.i.d. draws from \(F_1\) and \(F_0\), respectively, and their joint law is independent of \(W\sim\nu\).

novel.justification: Separate exposure-specific historical samples are available in insurance and public-health deployments even when privacy or record linkage prevents cross-arm pairing; independence from the later randomized assignment is ensured by collecting or freezing those archives before randomization. Mikhaeil and Green inform consistency of empirical marginal endpoints, not this product sampling law.

definitions.name: \mathcal B_Z
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal B_Z=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ \lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)>0,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where \([B]\) quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two columns and the predicates are ass:block-separable-basis and ass:basis-invertibility.

definitions.name: \mathcal B_\kappa
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal B_\kappa=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ (\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n),\ \lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), with the predicates ass:block-separable-basis, ass:projective-normalization, and ass:kappa-regularity.

definitions.name: h(c),g_B(c),\ell_B(c)
definitions.construction: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).

definitions.name: r(B),w(B),v^\star,v_{\mathrm{mm}}
definitions.construction: Retain \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) only as secondary maximin-gain diagnostics.  The primary robust loss and minimax value are \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).

definitions.name: \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}},\mathcal A_R,\mathcal A_0
definitions.construction: On the feasible covariance domain, where ass:product-coupling-zero and ass:frechet-covariance-domain give \(0\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\), retain \(\mathcal A_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) as the secondary maximin-gain correspondence, define the primary minimax-residual correspondence \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\), and define the ordinarily typed zero-covariance surrogate correspondence \(\mathcal A_0=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}
definitions.construction: Encode \(\Pi,\Omega,Q(c_L),Q(c_U),c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon\) either by exact rational or real-algebraic data, or by outward-rounded inclusion oracles supplied with effective refinement moduli and an exact decision oracle for sphere feasibility and the inequality \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa\), including equality at the \(\kappa\)-boundary.  Equivalently, the endpoint moment matrices may be encoded through \(\mu_1,\mu_0,\sigma_1^2,\sigma_0^2,c_L,c_U\).  Require \(\varepsilon\) itself to have an exact positive rational or real-algebraic encoding.

definitions.name: \mathscr K_{\varepsilon}
definitions.construction: A corrected minimax certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) consists of a finite quotient-chart cover, an exactly feasible incumbent \(B_{\varepsilon}\), rational bounds \(L_{\varepsilon},U_{\varepsilon}\), outward-rounded endpoint-loss and constraint bounds for every retained box, a checkable exact-infeasibility or valid lower-bound pruning record for every discarded box, retained boxes whose union is \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\), and their maximum chart diameter \(h_{\varepsilon}\).  The checker requires \(L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon}\), \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_\varepsilon\); it never accepts deletion of a box meeting the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary without an exact infeasibility certificate or a valid objective lower bound exceeding the incumbent upper bound.

definitions.name: candidate projective interval branch-and-bound handle
definitions.construction: Given the moment-complete \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\), the candidate projective interval branch-and-bound procedure covers each normalized projective factor by the finite pivot-coordinate charts \(\{|b_j|\ge n^{-1/2}\}\), bisects retained boxes, handles the sphere equations and exact \(\kappa\)-boundary through the feasibility interface, and bounds both endpoint residual losses and every constraint by outward-rounded interval extensions and interval-Hessian underestimators.  It maintains an exactly feasible incumbent and prunes only by exact infeasibility or by a certified box lower bound exceeding the incumbent upper bound.  Finite termination with \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), and the full outer-set certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) is an open proof obligation, not a property asserted by this construction.

definitions.name: \widehat w,\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}},\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}
definitions.construction: Compute the empirical means, variances, and two empirical quantile-coupling covariances from \(\widehat F_1,\widehat F_0\); substitute them into \(Q(c_L),Q(c_U)\), \(h(c)\), \(g_B(c)\), and \(\ell_B(c)\).  Retain the resulting \(\widehat r(B)\), \(\widehat v=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\) only as secondary diagnostics.  Define \(\widehat w(B)=\max\{\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_L),\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_U)\}\), \(\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B)\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B)\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak X_\kappa
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak X_\kappa=\{\xi=(\nu,F_1,F_0):\operatorname{ass{:}exposure\mbox{-}positivity}(\xi)\wedge\operatorname{ass{:}kappa\mbox{-}feasibility}(\xi)\wedge F_1,F_0\in\mathcal P([0,1])\}\) is carved by the single named positivity and feasibility predicates, with the relative topology inherited from total variation on the finite assignment simplex and the Wasserstein metric on each bounded marginal.

definitions.name: \Delta(\xi)
definitions.construction: \(\Delta(\xi)=\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi)}w_{\xi}(B_0)-\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)}w_{\xi}(B_{\mathrm{mm}})\).  Since every member of \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\) has loss \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\), the second term equals \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\).

definitions.name: finite lawful minimax separation handle
definitions.construction: Start from a three-vertex network under independent Bernoulli assignment with probability \(1/3\), enumerate the mutually exclusive exposure truth tables exactly, derive exact \(\Pi\) and \(\Omega\), use Bernoulli \(1/2\) pilot marginals, and apply the candidate certified projective interval handle simultaneously to the full minimax-residual and zero-covariance-surrogate correspondences.  Search for rational certificates \(\delta>0\) and \(\eta>0\) that bound \(\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0}w(B_0)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) from below and certify strict \(\kappa\)-slack over every member of \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\cup\mathcal A_0\).  No certificate is asserted until exact enumeration, full equality-set bounds, and the corrected finite-termination proof are supplied.

statements.statement: Under ass:known-exposure, ass:mutually-exclusive-exposures, ass:exposure-positivity, and ass:iid-potential-pairs, every \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) has affine functions \(c\mapsto g_B(c)\) and \(c\mapsto\ell_B(c)\) on the imported feasible domain \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\). Consequently, \(\inf_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}g_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}\ell_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\), with both extrema attained. The product coupling gives \(c_L\le0\le c_U\), so \(g_B(0)\) is an ordinarily typed feasible-covariance gain. If \(c_L<0<c_U\), \(g_B(0)=\inf_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}g_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})\) if and only if the affine slope of \(g_B\) is zero.
statements.justification: The theorem imports the published Fréchet range and proves its exact affine reduction inside Zhao's basis objective.
statements.gap: AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance, Lemma 1, already gives the sharp covariance range. Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates, Theorem 4 and equation (8) on pp. 22--23, gives the covariance-dependent basis objective, and the paragraph following Theorem 4 on p. 23 substitutes the feasible zero-covariance surrogate matrix; neither source derives the affine worst-copula and zero-surrogate frontier inside this projective objective.
statements.consumer: An experimenter with only two pilot marginals can evaluate the exact worst-copula gain of any proposed network basis.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
By ass:exposure-positivity, \(\Pi\) is invertible.  If \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\), the defining nondegeneracy condition gives \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\succ0\), so \(S_B^{-1}\) exists.  Put
\[
E=\begin{bmatrix}0&I_n\\ I_n&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
A_B=\Pi^{-1}\Omega B S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}.
\]
The moment-matrix construction gives \(Q(c)=Q(0)-cE\).  Cyclicity and linearity of trace yield
\[
g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\{A_BQ(0)\}
-c n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(A_BE),
\]
so \(g_B\) is affine.  The identity proved in lem:ht-affine-drift gives \(h(c)=h(0)+2c/n\).  Since def:gain-loss gives \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), \(\ell_B\) is affine as well.  Ass:known-exposure and ass:iid-potential-pairs supply the causal exposure and ex ante moment interpretations; the affine calculation itself uses only the stated matrix identities, with all inverses justified above.

By ass:frechet-covariance-domain and def:coupling-class,
\[
\left\{\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}:H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\right\}
=[c_L,c_U].
\]
An affine real function on this compact interval attains its minimum and maximum at an endpoint.  Equality of the covariance image with the entire closed interval also says that each endpoint is attained by a coupling in \(\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\).  Hence
\[
\inf_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
g_B\!\left(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}\right)
=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}
\]
and
\[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\ell_B\!\left(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}\right)
=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\},
\]
with both extrema attained.

By ass:product-coupling-zero, \(F_1\otimes F_0\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\) has covariance zero.  Thus ass:frechet-covariance-domain gives \(0\in[c_L,c_U]\), or \(c_L\le0\le c_U\), and \(g_B(0)\) is ordinarily typed.

Finally write \(g_B(c)=\alpha_B+\beta_Bc\).  If \(\beta_B=0\), then \(g_B\) is constant and its value at zero is its worst-coupling value.  Conversely suppose \(c_L<0<c_U\).  If \(\beta_B>0\), then \(g_B(c_L)=g_B(0)+\beta_Bc_L<g_B(0)\); if \(\beta_B<0\), then \(g_B(c_U)=g_B(0)+\beta_Bc_U<g_B(0)\).  Thus equality with the infimum is possible only when \(\beta_B=0\). \(\square\)

statements.statement: For every \(\kappa>0\), the quotient \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is compact and satisfies \(\mathcal B_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\).  Conversely, every \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) has normalized representatives belonging to \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) for some basis-dependent \(\kappa>0\), so \(\bigcup_{\kappa>0}\mathcal B_\kappa=\mathcal B_Z\).  Here \(\mathcal B_Z\) is the nondegenerate ordinary-inverse projective repair of the block-diagonal Zhao domain: the union statement covers every nonsingular implementable Zhao-type basis through a basis-dependent threshold, but it neither identifies any fixed \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) with the published class nor covers singular or pseudoinverse bases.
statements.justification: The proposition states exactly what the computational regularity restriction loses and recovers.
statements.gap: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates, Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 21, imposes boundedness and \(\lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\lambda_\Omega n\) on a supplied basis, but does not establish existence of a normalized feasible basis or construct a compact projective exhaustion for global optimization.
statements.consumer: Certified solvers can report the regularity threshold alongside the basis instead of presenting an undocumented numerical trim.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let
\[
K_\kappa=\left\{(b_1,b_0):
\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n,
\ \lambda_{\min}\!\left(n^{-1}B(b_1,b_0)^{\top}\Omega B(b_1,b_0)\right)\ge\kappa
\right\}.
\]
The product of the two radius-\(\sqrt n\) spheres is compact.  The matrix map in this display and the smallest-eigenvalue map are continuous, so \(K_\kappa\) is closed and compact, including when it is empty.  The quotient map identifying independent nonzero column rescalings is continuous; def:kappa-basis-class therefore makes \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) its compact image.

Every member of \(K_\kappa\) satisfies
\[
\lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge n\kappa>0,
\]
so def:zhao-basis-class gives \(\mathcal B_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\).

Conversely, take \([B]\in\mathcal B_Z\), represented by \(B=B(b_1,b_0)\).  Positive definiteness of \(S_B\) forces \(b_1,b_0\ne0\).  Put
\[
d_a=\frac{\sqrt n}{\lVert b_a\rVert_2},
\qquad T=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,d_0),
\qquad \widetilde B=BT.
\]
Then \(\widetilde B\) is a normalized representative of the same projective class and
\[
S_{\widetilde B}=T S_BT\succ0.
\]
Thus \(\rho_B=\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_{\widetilde B})>0\).  With \(\kappa_B=\rho_B/2\), the representative belongs to \(\mathcal B_{\kappa_B}\).  This proves \(\bigcup_{\kappa>0}\mathcal B_\kappa=\mathcal B_Z\).

The conclusion is exactly an exhaustion of the nondegenerate ordinary-inverse quotient defined in def:zhao-basis-class.  Since the threshold obtained above depends on \(B\), it does not identify a fixed \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) with Zhao's unrestricted block-diagonal domain; and because the argument starts from \(S_B\succ0\), it says nothing about singular or pseudoinverse bases. \(\square\)

statements.statement: If \(\xi_0\in\mathfrak X_\kappa\) satisfies \(\Delta(\xi_0)>0\) and there is \(\eta>0\) such that \(\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\cup\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}\{\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)-\kappa\}\ge\eta\), then there is a relative-open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) of \(\xi_0\) such that \(\Delta(\xi)>0\) for every \(\xi\in\mathcal U\).
statements.justification: Persistence upgrades any exact finite witness from a curiosity to a nondegenerate region of lawful experiments.
statements.gap: Bergin1999RestrictedMarginals gives continuity of fixed-marginal coupling correspondences, while GaoKleywegt2017DependenceRobust gives a general dependence-robust decision template; neither proves strict robust-basis dominance for Zhao's optimizer correspondences.
statements.consumer: Any certified output of oeq:separated-lawful-witness with \(\delta>0\) and optimizer-wide slack \(\eta>0\) activates this theorem and yields a relative-open region on which every robust optimizer has lower worst-copula residual variance than every zero-covariance-surrogate optimizer.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Write \(K(\xi)=\mathcal B_\kappa(\xi)\).  On the finite assignment space, total-variation convergence \(\nu_j\to\nu\) implies entrywise convergence of \(\Pi_j\) and \(\Omega_j\).  At an exposure-positive instance the diagonal entries of \(\Pi\) are positive, so \(\Pi_j^{-1}\to\Pi^{-1}\).  If \(F_{a,j}\to F_a\) in Wasserstein distance on \([0,1]\), the quantile representation of that distance gives
\[
\int_0^1|F_{a,j}^{-1}(u)-F_a^{-1}(u)|\,du\longrightarrow0.
\tag{1}
\]
All quantiles lie in \([0,1]\), whence
\[
\left|\int_0^1q_{1,j}(u)q_{0,j}(u)\,du-
\int_0^1q_1(u)q_0(u)\,du\right|
\le\lVert q_{1,j}-q_1\rVert_1+\lVert q_{0,j}-q_0\rVert_1,
\tag{2}
\]
with the same bound for the reflected second quantile.  Marginal first and second moments also converge.  Thus \(c_L,c_U,Q(c_L),Q(c_U)\) vary continuously with \(\xi\).

On the product of normalized spheres, both
\[
(\xi,B)\longmapsto\lambda_{\min}\{n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega(\xi)B\}
\tag{3}
\]
and the endpoint formulas are continuous.  On the superlevel set in (3), \(\lVert S_B^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le(n\kappa)^{-1}\).  It follows that
\[
(\xi,B)\longmapsto g_{B,\xi}(0),
\qquad
(\xi,B)\longmapsto w_\xi(B)
\tag{4}
\]
are jointly continuous on the feasible graph.

We next prove upper stability of both optimizer correspondences.  Let \(\xi_j\to\xi_0\), let \(B_j\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_j)\), and suppose \(B_j\to B\) along a subsequence in the compact normalized quotient.  Closedness of (3) gives \(B\in K(\xi_0)\).  Choose \(B^\circ\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\).  The slack hypothesis gives
\[
\lambda_{\min}\{n^{-1}S_{B^\circ}(\xi_0)\}\ge\kappa+\eta,
\]
so continuity makes the fixed basis \(B^\circ\) feasible at every sufficiently large \(j\).  Optimality and (4) give
\[
w_{\xi_j}(B_j)\le w_{\xi_j}(B^\circ)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
w_{\xi_0}(B)\le w_{\xi_0}(B^\circ)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0).
\]
Feasibility supplies the reverse inequality, hence \(B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\).  The same argument, with the inequality reversed and with \(g(0)\) in place of \(w\), proves upper stability of \(\mathcal A_0\).  The optimizer-wide slack is used exactly to keep the fixed comparison optimizer feasible under perturbation.

The optimizer sets are nonempty and compact.  For each \(j\), select
\[
B_{0,j}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_j)}w_{\xi_j}(B),
\qquad
B_{\mathrm{mm},j}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_j)}w_{\xi_j}(B).
\]
Every subsequence has a further subsequence on which both bases converge.  Upper stability and (4) put the limits in the corresponding optimizer sets at \(\xi_0\).  Therefore
\[
\liminf_{j\to\infty}\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_j)}w_{\xi_j}(B)
\ge\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B)
\tag{5}
\]
and
\[
\limsup_{j\to\infty}\sup_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_j)}w_{\xi_j}(B)
\le\sup_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B).
\tag{6}
\]
Subtracting (6) from (5) gives \(\liminf_j\Delta(\xi_j)\ge\Delta(\xi_0)>0\).  If no relative-open neighborhood with positive gap existed, metrizability of the stated product topology would give a sequence \(\xi_j\to\xi_0\) with \(\Delta(\xi_j)\le0\), a contradiction. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Can the construction in def:separation-search-handle produce explicit \(G\), exposure maps \(f_i\), assignment law \(\nu\), marginals \(F_1,F_0\), and threshold \(\kappa\), together with exact \(\Pi,\Omega,Q(c_L),Q(c_U),c_L,c_U\), checkable exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility certificates, and rational \(\delta,\eta>0\) such that the induced \(\xi_0\in\mathfrak X_\kappa\) satisfies
\[
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B_0)
-\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B_{\mathrm{mm}})\ge\delta
\]
and
\[
\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\cup\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}
\{\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)-\kappa\}\ge\eta,
\]
with both bounds certified over the full minimax-residual and zero-covariance optimizer correspondences?
statements.justification: This correspondence-level certificate is the early kill test for whether strict minimax-residual dominance and the persistence hypothesis hold at any lawful finite design.
statements.gap: No located paper or current core result supplies a lawful network instance with a certified positive separation between the full minimax-residual and zero-covariance optimizer correspondences; a hand-picked pair of bases would not establish the required claim.
statements.consumer: Only a positive separation-and-slack certificate licenses the downstream open-neighborhood result and a strict-dominance interpretation in the Jiangxi application.

statements.statement: Fix \(G,\nu,(f_i)_{i=1}^n\) satisfying ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility, so \(\mathcal B_\kappa\neq\varnothing\).  Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot, as \(m_1\wedge m_0\to\infty\), \(\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|\to0\) almost surely, \(\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}\to v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) almost surely, and every subsequential limit of \(B_m\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) almost surely.  Equivalently, \(\limsup_{m_1,m_0\to\infty}\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) almost surely in the projective quotient.
statements.justification: The set-valued conclusion is the strongest valid generic guarantee when projective symmetries or endpoint ties create multiple optimizers.
statements.gap: AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance and MikhaeilGreen2024SharpRegressionAdjustment prove scalar endpoint consistency; Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates, Theorem 3, concerns estimated-coefficient consistency and asymptotics but does not establish uniform global basis-objective or argmax-correspondence consistency.
statements.consumer: An independent historical or external pilot can select a robust network basis without pretending that its two marginal samples identify a cross-world copula.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix normalized representatives of the projective classes in \(\mathcal B_\kappa\).  By prop:kappa-exhaustion and ass:kappa-feasibility, this is a nonempty compact space.  The two columns of every representative have disjoint block supports and squared norm \(n\), while feasibility gives
\[
\lVert B\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=\sqrt n,
\qquad
\lVert S_B^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le(n\kappa)^{-1}.
\tag{1}
\]
Exposure positivity makes \(\Pi^{-1}\) well defined, and all design matrices are fixed.

Write \(q_a=F_a^{-1}\) and \(\widehat q_a=\widehat F_a^{-1}\).  We first derive convergence of every pilot ingredient.  If \(X_j\) are independent, centered, and \(|X_j|\le1\), expansion of the fourth moment gives
\[
\mathbb E\left(\sum_{j=1}^mX_j\right)^4
\le 3m^2.
\]
Markov's inequality and summability of \(3/(m^2t^4)\) imply the bounded strong law by the Borel--Cantelli argument.  Apply it to the outcomes, their squares, and, simultaneously over rational \(x\), the indicators \(\mathbf1\{Y^P_{j,a}\le x\}\).  Monotonicity then gives empirical-distribution convergence at all continuity points.  The generalized-inverse squeeze gives \(\widehat q_a(u)\to q_a(u)\) at every continuity point of \(q_a\).  Since monotone functions have at most countably many discontinuities and all quantiles lie in \([0,1]\), dominated convergence yields
\[
\lVert\widehat q_a-q_a\rVert_{L^1(0,1)}\longrightarrow0,
\quad
\widehat\mu_a\longrightarrow\mu_a,
\quad
\widehat\sigma_a^2\longrightarrow\sigma_a^2
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{2}
\]
Because all quantiles are bounded by one,
\[
\left|\int_0^1\widehat q_1(u)\widehat q_0(u)\,du-
\int_0^1q_1(u)q_0(u)\,du\right|
\le\lVert\widehat q_1-q_1\rVert_1+
\lVert\widehat q_0-q_0\rVert_1,
\tag{3}
\]
and the same inequality holds after replacing the second quantile by its reflection at \(1-u\).  Thus
\[
\widehat c_L\to c_L,
\qquad \widehat c_U\to c_U
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{4}
\]
For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), let \(Q_e=Q(c_e)\) and let \(\widehat Q_e\) be its plug-in counterpart.  Equations (2)--(4) and the finite-dimensional formula in def:moment-matrix imply
\[
\rho_m:=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}
\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q_e\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{5}
\]

Put \(C_\nu=\lVert\Omega\Pi^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\) and \(A_{\mathrm{HT}}=\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\).  The inequality \(|\operatorname{tr}(M)|\le d\lVert M\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\) for a \(d\times d\) matrix, def:gain-loss, and (1) give, uniformly in \(B\),
\[
\max_e|\widehat g_{B,e}-g_{B,e}|
\le \frac{2C_\nu^2}{n^2\kappa}\rho_m,
\qquad
\max_e|\widehat h_e-h_e|
\le \frac{2}{n}\lVert A_{\mathrm{HT}}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\rho_m.
\tag{6}
\]
Therefore \(\max_e|\widehat\ell_{B,e}-\ell_{B,e}|\) is bounded by the sum of the two right sides in (6), uniformly in \(B\).  Since the maximum of two coordinates is one-Lipschitz in the sup norm,
\[
\delta_m:=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}
|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{7}
\]

Each endpoint loss is continuous on \(\mathcal B_\kappa\), because inversion is continuous on the uniformly positive-definite set in (1); hence \(w\) and \(\widehat w\) attain their minima.  The elementary minimum inequality gives
\[
|\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}-v_{\mathrm{mm}}|
\le\delta_m\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{8}
\]
Finally, take \(B_m\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and a convergent subsequence \(B_{m_j}\to B_\infty\), which exists by compactness.  For any \(B^\star\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\), empirical optimality and (7) give
\[
w(B_{m_j})
\le\widehat w(B_{m_j})+\delta_{m_j}
\le\widehat w(B^\star)+\delta_{m_j}
\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}+2\delta_{m_j}.
\]
Continuity and the defining lower bound \(w\ge v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) imply \(w(B_\infty)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}\), so \(B_\infty\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\).  This is precisely the asserted one-sided outer-limit inclusion. \(\square\)

statements.statement: If \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\{B^\star\}\) in the projective quotient, \(B^\star\) is isolated by a positive loss gap outside every neighborhood, and exactly one of \(c_L,c_U\) attains \(w(B^\star)\), then every measurable selection \(\widehat B\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\) converges almost surely to \(B^\star\).  Without the singleton condition, there exist bounded two-marginal instances satisfying the maintained assumptions for which the outer-set conclusion of thm:plugin-correspondence holds but some measurable plug-in selections fail to converge to a point.
statements.justification: This proposition draws the exact line between defensible set consistency and unjustified point consistency.
statements.gap: Bergin1999RestrictedMarginals implies upper hemicontinuity for optimizer sets but does not give this pilot-based quotient-space selection result or its tie counterexample.
statements.consumer: Applied reporting can retain all empirically indistinguishable robust bases unless an isolated unique saddle is actually verified.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Work on the probability-one event on which thm:plugin-correspondence holds, and let \(U\) be any neighborhood of \(B^\star\).  The asserted isolation gives
\[
\gamma_U:=\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa\setminus U}w(B)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}>0.
\tag{1}
\]
Let \(\delta_m=\sup_B|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|\), so \(\delta_m\to0\).  If \(2\delta_m<\gamma_U\), then every \(B\notin U\) satisfies
\[
\widehat w(B)\ge w(B)-\delta_m
\ge v_{\mathrm{mm}}+\gamma_U-\delta_m
>v_{\mathrm{mm}}+\delta_m
\ge\widehat w(B^\star).
\]
Consequently \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\subset U\) eventually.  Since \(U\) was arbitrary, every measurable selection converges almost surely to \(B^\star\).  The unique active endpoint labels the limiting saddle; once singleton isolation is assumed, it is not needed for convergence of the basis itself.

For the failure of point convergence under ties, let \(n=3\), take \(f_i(w)=w_i\), and let the coordinates of \(W\) be independent Bernoulli \(1/2\).  Then
\[
\Pi=\frac12I_6,
\qquad
\Omega=\frac14\begin{bmatrix}I_3&-I_3\\-I_3&I_3\end{bmatrix}.
\tag{2}
\]
Let \(F_1=F_0=\delta_0\), let \(H=\delta_{(0,0)}\), and use the corresponding unpaired pilots.  Then
\[
\mu_1=\mu_0=\sigma_1^2=\sigma_0^2=c_L=c_U=0,
\qquad Q(0)=0.
\tag{3}
\]
Choose \(\kappa=1/8\) and, with \(e_j\) the coordinate vectors of \(\mathbb R^3\), define
\[
B^{(2)}=B(\sqrt3e_1,\sqrt3e_2),
\qquad B^{(3)}=B(\sqrt3e_1,\sqrt3e_3).
\]
For \(j\in\{2,3\}\), (2) gives
\[
S_{B^{(j)}}=\frac34I_2,
\qquad
\lambda_{\min}\{3^{-1}S_{B^{(j)}}\}=\frac14>\kappa.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus the two displayed bases are distinct feasible projective points.  By (3), however, \(h(0)=g_B(0)=\ell_B(0)=w(B)=0\) for every feasible \(B\).  Every pilot observation is identically zero, so the same equalities hold empirically and
\[
\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}
=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\mathcal B_\kappa
\quad\text{at every pilot size}.
\tag{5}
\]
Along \(m_1=m_0=m\), select \(B^{(2)}\) for even \(m\) and \(B^{(3)}\) for odd \(m\).  This deterministic measurable selection has two distinct subsequential limits, while (5) makes the outer-set conclusion exact. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Endpoint covariances alone do not determine the minimax worst-copula residual value.  In particular, let \(n=3\), let \(W_1,W_2,W_3\) be independent Bernoulli \(1/2\) variables under \(\nu\), and set \(f_i(w)=w_i\).  With \(\kappa=1/8\) and \(\varepsilon=1/100\), the marginal pairs \((F_1,F_0)=(\delta_0,\delta_0)\) and \((F_1,F_0)=(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2),\delta_0)\) produce the same moment-incomplete tuple
\[
\Pi=\tfrac12 I_6,\qquad
\Omega=\tfrac14\begin{bmatrix}I_3&-I_3\\-I_3&I_3\end{bmatrix},
\qquad c_L=c_U=0,
\]
but their endpoint moment matrices differ and their minimax residual values are, respectively,
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=\frac1{36}.
\]
Consequently, no algorithm whose only input is \((\Pi,\Omega,c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon)\) can always return rational bounds
\[
L_{\varepsilon}\le \min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\le U_{\varepsilon},
\qquad U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon.
\]
Thus endpoint moment matrices such as \(Q(c_L)\) and \(Q(c_U)\), or equivalent marginal moments, are necessary inputs for the proposed certification problem.  This obstruction makes no claim that the corrected moment-complete branch-and-bound solver terminates at every positive tolerance.
statements.proof_tex:
\paragraph{Proof.}
Write \(J_3=\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}\) and
\[
K=\begin{bmatrix}I_3&-I_3\\-I_3&I_3\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Because \(f_i(W)=W_i\), the two exposure indicators are \(D_{i,1}=W_i\) and \(D_{i,0}=1-W_i\).  They are mutually exclusive on every assignment.  Independence and \(\operatorname{Var}_{\nu}(W_i)=1/4\) therefore give, entry by entry,
\[
\Pi=\tfrac12 I_6,
\qquad
\Omega=\operatorname{Var}_{\nu}(D)=\tfrac14K.
\]
Exposure positivity holds because every diagonal entry of \(\Pi\) is \(1/2\), so \(\Pi^{-1}=2I_6\) exists.

We next verify that the normalized regular basis class is nonempty and that the witness is away from its boundary.  Set
\[
b_1=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&1\end{bmatrix}^{\top},
\qquad
b_0=\sqrt{\tfrac32}\begin{bmatrix}1&-1&0\end{bmatrix}^{\top}.
\]
Then \(\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=3\) and \(b_1^{\top}b_0=0\).  For the associated block-separable basis,
\[
S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B
=\tfrac14
\begin{bmatrix}
3&-b_1^{\top}b_0\\
-b_0^{\top}b_1&3
\end{bmatrix}
=\tfrac34I_2.
\]
Hence \(\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)=1/4>1/8=\kappa\).  This proves feasibility and the rank condition rather than assuming them; in particular, every inverse used below exists for every \(B\in\mathcal B_\kappa\).

For \((F_1,F_0)=(\delta_0,\delta_0)\), all four marginal means and variances vanish.  Both quantile products vanish, so \(c_L=c_U=0\), and the moment-matrix definition gives \(Q(0)=0\).  Therefore \(\ell_B(0)=0\) for every \(B\in\mathcal B_\kappa\), whence
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=0.
\]

Now take \((F_1,F_0)=(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2),\delta_0)\).  Both marginals are supported on \([0,1]\).  Since the comparison potential outcome is constant, every coupling has covariance zero; equivalently, direct evaluation of both quantile integrals gives \(c_L=c_U=0\).  Here
\[
\mu_1=\tfrac12,
\quad \sigma_1^2=\tfrac14,
\quad \mu_0=\sigma_0^2=0,
\quad
Q(0)=\begin{bmatrix}A&0\\0&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
A=\tfrac14(I_3+J_3).
\]
Thus the two marginal pairs have the same displayed moment-incomplete tuple, although their endpoint moment matrices are different.

It remains to calculate the second minimax residual exactly.  Let \(B\in\mathcal B_\kappa\) be arbitrary, write \(x=b_1\), \(y=b_0\), and put \(C=[x,-y]\).  Projective normalization gives \(\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3\).  Moreover, \(\kappa\)-regularity makes \(S_B\) positive definite, so \(C\) has rank two.  Direct block multiplication, using \(\Pi^{-1}=2I_6\) and \(\Omega=K/4\), yields
\[
S_B=\tfrac14C^{\top}C,
\qquad
B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(0)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B
=\tfrac14C^{\top}AC.
\]
Consequently, if
\[
P_C=C(C^{\top}C)^{-1}C^{\top}
\]
denotes the rank-two orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{col}(C)\), cyclicity of trace gives
\[
g_B(0)
=\tfrac19\operatorname{tr}\!\left[(C^{\top}C)^{-1}C^{\top}AC\right]
=\tfrac19\operatorname{tr}(P_CA).
\]
The basis-free term in the residual is
\[
h(0)
:=\tfrac19\operatorname{tr}\!\left[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(0)\right]
=\tfrac19\operatorname{tr}(A)
=\tfrac16.
\]
Let \(u=3^{-1/2}\mathbf 1\).  Since \(J_3=3uu^{\top}\),
\[
A=\tfrac14I_3+\tfrac34uu^{\top}.
\]
Because \(P_C\) is an orthogonal projector of rank two,
\[
\operatorname{tr}(P_CA)
=\tfrac14\operatorname{tr}(P_C)+\tfrac34u^{\top}P_Cu
=\tfrac12+\tfrac34\lVert P_Cu\rVert_2^2
\le\tfrac54.
\]
It follows for every feasible basis that
\[
\ell_B(0)=h(0)-g_B(0)
\ge\tfrac16-\tfrac19\cdot\tfrac54
=\tfrac1{36}.
\]
The previously displayed feasible choice has \(b_1=\sqrt3u\) and \(b_0\perp u\), so \(u\in\operatorname{col}(C)\), \(\lVert P_Cu\rVert_2=1\), and equality holds throughout.  Because the covariance interval is the singleton \(\{0\}\), \(w(B)=\ell_B(0)\), proving
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=\tfrac1{36}.
\]

Finally, an algorithm receiving only the displayed moment-incomplete tuple must return the same \((L_{\varepsilon},U_{\varepsilon})\) on these two instances.  Validity on both would force \([L_{\varepsilon},U_{\varepsilon}]\) to contain both \(0\) and \(1/36\), so
\[
U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\ge\tfrac1{36}>\tfrac1{100}=\varepsilon,
\]
contradicting the required tolerance.  The contradiction concerns only omission of the endpoint moment matrices and therefore does not establish existence or finite termination of the repaired moment-complete solver.

The causal estimand remains the finite-population exposure contrast \(\tau\).  The minimax residual is an ex ante design criterion for choosing a control-variate basis; it is not an identifying formula for \(\tau\).  \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Let \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\).  Under ass:mutually-exclusive-exposures, ass:exposure-positivity, ass:frechet-covariance-domain, and ass:product-coupling-zero,
\[
h(c)=h(0)+\frac{2c}{n}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
w(B)=h(0)+\max\left\{\frac{2c_L}{n}-g_B(c_L),\frac{2c_U}{n}-g_B(c_U)\right\}.
\]
If \(c_L<c_U\), minimization of \(w(B)\) is not algebraically equivalent to maximization of \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\): as functions of a formal endpoint-gain pair \((x_L,x_U)\), the two loss criteria are not related by a constant independent of \((x_L,x_U)\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Set
\[
E=\begin{bmatrix}0&I_n\\ I_n&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad A_{\mathrm{HT}}=\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}.
\]
By def:moment-matrix, \(Q(c)=Q(0)-cE\).  For each unit \(i\), ass:mutually-exclusive-exposures gives \(D_{i,1}D_{i,0}=0\) almost surely.  Hence
\[
\Omega_{i,n+i}=\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu}(D_{i,1},D_{i,0})
=-\pi_{i,1}\pi_{i,0}.
\]
Ass:exposure-positivity permits division by both probabilities.  Since \(A_{\mathrm{HT}}\) is symmetric,
\[
\operatorname{tr}(A_{\mathrm{HT}}E)
=2\sum_{i=1}^n
\frac{\Omega_{i,n+i}}{\pi_{i,1}\pi_{i,0}}
=-2n.
\]
Therefore cyclicity and linearity of trace imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
h(c)
&=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\{A_{\mathrm{HT}}(Q(0)-cE)\}\\
&=h(0)-cn^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(A_{\mathrm{HT}}E)
=h(0)+\frac{2c}{n}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Substitution into \(w(B)=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\{h(c_e)-g_B(c_e)\}\) proves the displayed expression for \(w\).

It remains to make the non-equivalence precise.  Put \(a_e=2c_e/n\) and, for a formal pair \(x=(x_L,x_U)\), define
\[
F(x)=\max\{a_L-x_L,a_U-x_U\},
\qquad G(x)=\max\{-x_L,-x_U\}.
\]
Minimizing worst residual uses \(F\), up to the constant \(h(0)\), whereas maximizing minimum gain is equivalent to minimizing \(G=-\min\{x_L,x_U\}\).  If \(F(x)=G(x)+K\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^2\), then taking \((x_L,x_U)=(t,0)\) and sending \(t\to\infty\) gives \(K=a_U\); taking \((x_L,x_U)=(0,t)\) gives \(K=a_L\).  Thus such an algebraic identity requires \(a_L=a_U\), equivalently \(c_L=c_U\).  When \(c_L<c_U\), no such identity exists. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Suppose ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility hold.  The primary minimax correspondence is nonempty and satisfies the unconditional weak worst-copula dominance certificate
\[
\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}}w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm}}
\le
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0}w(B_0).
\]
Strict inequality is not universal and requires a separate lawful witness.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
By ass:kappa-feasibility and prop:kappa-exhaustion, \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is nonempty and compact.  Exposure positivity makes \(\Pi^{-1}\) well defined, and membership in \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) gives \(S_B\succeq n\kappa I_2\), so inversion is continuous throughout this compact class.  The finite-dimensional formulas in def:gain-loss therefore make \(w\) and \(B\mapsto g_B(0)\) continuous.  Consequently both \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and \(\mathcal A_0\) are nonempty compact sets.

For every \(B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and every \(B_0\in\mathcal A_0\), the defining minimum gives
\[
w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})=v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_0).
\]
The left side is constant over \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\).  Taking the supremum over \(B_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and then the infimum over \(B_0\) proves the certificate.  The argument yields only a weak inequality; equality can occur, for example when both marginals are point masses and all endpoint moment matrices vanish. \(\square\)

sampling_model.design: A fixed finite network \(G\), known assignment law \(\nu\), known exposure maps \(f_i\), and two mutually exclusive exposure events.
sampling_model.units: The realized finite-population potential outcomes are fixed for design-based estimation; the i.i.d. law \(H\) is used only to choose the basis ex ante.
sampling_model.treatment: The main experiment draws \(W\sim\nu\), and assignment is the only randomness in the causal estimator conditional on the chosen basis.
sampling_model.overlap: Every exposure probability \(\pi_{i,a}\) is positive, and basis covariance is bounded below by \(\kappa\) on the optimization class.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Two arm-specific external or historical i.i.d. samples are mutually unpaired and independent of the later assignment; they estimate \(F_1\) and \(F_0\), while the cross-world copula is neither estimated nor assumed.

comparator_promise_table.matched_by: thm:fixed-basis-endpoints and thm:minimax-residual-weak-dominance on the nondegenerate repaired quotient and fixed regularized subclass

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Comonotone and countermonotone quantile couplings attain sharp covariance and variance endpoints for fixed marginals.
Empirical adjusted-outcome marginals consistently estimate sharp regression-adjusted variance endpoints.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Branch-and-bound can attain finite global guarantees for bounded nonconvex all-quadratic programs.

tldr: Rare network exposures make Horvitz--Thompson estimation noisy, and Zhao's optimal indicator control variates reduce this design variance, but the ex ante basis depends on a cross-world covariance that an unpaired pilot cannot identify. The contribution chain imports the sharp Fréchet covariance range, proves a new fixed-basis affine worst-copula reduction inside Zhao's objective, poses certified global maximin optimization on the fixed-\(\kappa\) projective class, and proves uniform plug-in value and outer argmax-correspondence consistency without assuming away ties. Neighborhood persistence is supporting and witness-gated; no strict-dominance region is claimed unless the full-correspondence separation-and-slack certificate is produced.

project_justification.gap: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates explicitly leaves robust basis choice under moment misspecification open; existing Fréchet results identify covariance endpoints, and existing global-optimization results certify Euclidean-box programs, but no paper joins these steps for a block-separable network basis with projective symmetry.
project_justification.niche: Two unpaired pilot marginals identify the exact dependence ambiguity relevant to Zhao's moment matrix while leaving the experimental network and assignment law fixed and known.
project_justification.fill: The project imports the sharp endpoint formulas, proves their affine worst-copula and zero-surrogate frontier inside Zhao's fixed-basis objective, formulates a computably specified global maximin certificate on the compact \(\kappa\)-regular projective class, and proves uniform plug-in value and outer argmax-correspondence consistency. Conditional persistence is supporting: a strict-dominance region requires a separate certified witness with both separation and optimizer-wide \(\kappa\)-slack.

related_work: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates is the direct anchor. Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 21 regulates a supplied basis, Assumption 3\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 22 supplies the i.i.d. potential-outcome-pair model, Theorem 4 and equation (8) on pp. 22--23 give the covariance-dependent basis optimization, and the paragraph following Theorem 4 on p. 23 gives the zero-covariance surrogate; Theorem 3 is limited to estimated-coefficient consistency and asymptotics. AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance is imported background: Lemma 1 proves the sharp covariance range and its quantile-coupling attainment, while Proposition 1 establishes endpoint estimation. The product coupling \(F_1\otimes F_0\) is feasible and has covariance zero, so Zhao's surrogate is an ordinarily typed member of the same covariance domain. MikhaeilGreen2024SharpRegressionAdjustment informs empirical marginal-endpoint consistency through Proposition 1, but neither supplies the independent unpaired product sampling law nor treats interference and an ex ante basis argmax. Bergin1999RestrictedMarginals informs continuity of fixed-marginal coupling correspondences. Reeves1975GlobalQuadratic and AdjimanDallwigFloudasNeumaier1998AlphaBB inform the incumbent, region-bound, subdivision, and convex-underestimator logic, but do not cover the projective quotient, exact regularity boundary, or endpoint kink. HarshawMiddletonSavje2026 optimizes conservative quadratic variance bounds under interference; its object is the variance bound rather than the control-variate basis. GaoKleywegt2017DependenceRobust informs the decision-theoretic treatment of dependence ambiguity but studies generic stochastic losses. AronowSamii2017 supplies the exposure-mapping design foundation. CaiDeJanvrySadoulet2015 is the application source for the Jiangxi insurance network that Zhao reanalyzes.
technical_internal_limitation: The presolve fractions \(521/1200\), \(2613/8432\), and \(4912/39525\) are not formal claims because the triangle exposure truth tables, the resulting entries of \(\Pi\) and \(\Omega\), the value of \(\kappa\), full equality-set bounds, and optimizer-wide strict \(\kappa\)-slack certificate are not supplied. The early kill test is oeq:separated-lawful-witness over exact assignment enumeration and both full optimizer correspondences. Unnumbered sanity check and regression test: if \(F_1\) and \(F_0\) are point masses, then the definitions give \(c_L=c_U=0\), hence \(r(B)=g_B(0)\) and \(\mathcal A_R=\mathcal A_0\). Zhao's Corollary 3 supports the stronger noiseless inverse-probability-weighted basis special case, while this correspondence equality is only a definitional code check and carries no theorem or novelty status.
honest_scope: The sharp Fréchet covariance range is imported from AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance, Lemma 1. The new theorem targets are its affine worst-copula reduction inside Zhao's fixed-basis objective, projective compactness, uniform plug-in value and outer-set consistency, and conditional neighborhood persistence. The finite epsilon-global solver and the separated lawful witness are first-class open constructions. Persistence is incremental and yields a strict-dominance region only after the witness supplies both a positive full-correspondence separation and optimizer-wide \(\kappa\)-slack; no such region is otherwise claimed. No SDP reduction, universal minimax interchange, universal strict improvement, asymptotic normality for the pilot-selected basis, or point convergence under ties is claimed.
